annotations.title: Look up a service by name

description: Search the Agent Nexus registry when you already know the service, product, vendor, slug or endpoint you are looking for. Use this for a targeted lookup, not for discovering a solution to a broad task; for a plain-language goal, use discover_capabilities instead. Matches literal text only and does not interpret intent. Optionally narrow the search by category. Returns {count, results[]} containing summary records with slug, name, category, summary, endpoint and trust fields. Results are alphabetical, not ranked by relevance. There is no pagination beyond the limit parameter: increase limit (maximum 50) or narrow the query when needed. Use get_entry to inspect the full record of a relevant result. An empty results[] is a valid answer, not an error. Read-only and side-effect free.

category.description: Optional filter, exactly one of 'api', 'mcp' or 'cli' (see list_categories). Combined with query as AND. Omit to search all three layers.

limit.description: Upper bound on entries returned, 1-50, default 10. Results are ordered by name, not by relevance, so a small limit on a broad keyword can hide better matches — raise it or use discover_capabilities when you are ranking candidates.

query.description: Literal substring, max 120 chars, matched case-insensitively against name, summary, endpoint and slug — a product name ('resend'), a vendor, a slug fragment or a host ('api.stripe.com'). Single terms work best: the whole string is matched as one substring, so 'send email' finds nothing unless those words appear together. The characters % , ( ) are stripped. An empty query (the default) returns the first entries in name order, which is a browse, not a search.

name: search_registry
title: Look up a service by name
